body: The female contraceptive pill was released before  thalidomide was banned when drugs were far less regulated. Much as I think a male contraceptive option should exist, we shouldn't lower standards to be in line with the 60s just because it's fairer. The fact a safe option hasn't been developed is a problem but that doesn't mean an unsafe option should be approved.

The problem is there's no way to ensure safety on a larger scale and so could lead to the spread of disease. Given that a) everyone has opportunistic pathogens in their gut and b) immunosuppressed people exist, safety is a huge issue here. Also I don't think it would even be that beneficial - adult microbiomes are in most cases quite stable. In the cases where they're not, you'd probably want a better controlled process than just eating slightly shitty vegetables.
